articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Unbeaten Mossdeep meets Saffron for the Indigo Bowl
articles.dek: The Eclipse won 20–17 in the regular season. Both finalists have brought more ways to finish drives into the playoffs, and each has a defense capable of taking those chances away.

body.text: Mossdeep and Saffron have already played a game in which one more touchdown would have changed the result. The Eclipse won 20–17 in Week 10, scoring from six yards out on the snap that began with 49 seconds left after trailing 17–6 at halftime. The teams meet again for the Indigo Bowl, this time on neutral ground. Mossdeep has won all 19 games it has played. Saffron finished the regular season 14–3 and added three playoff wins, including a victory over the Mt. Silver team that beat it in Week 15.

The deciding matchup is what the offenses can do once they’re in reach of the end zone and a pass rush can end the drive with one bad down. Saffron’s lead in the first game came from finishing two touchdown possessions while Mossdeep twice settled for kicks. Mossdeep reversed that in the second half, with two touchdowns from Accel BeckhmJr and no points allowed. Both clubs scored five touchdowns in their conference championships. I’m looking for which one can preserve that finishing edge against a defense that has already taken it away for a half.

Mossdeep has the larger body of evidence. It scored 724 regular-season points and allowed 130. Saffron posted 597 and 138. The defensive totals are close enough to make the difference in offensive scoring more interesting. Each club has already shown it can take away the sort of afternoon the other usually gets. The neutral final gives us a direct comparison without carrying over the location of the first meeting.

body.title: Season 1 finalists through the conference championships

body.text: How Mossdeep can finish against Saffron

My conference prediction gave Sunyshore 17 points. The Starseekers scored 31, and they made Mossdeep answer five separate scoring possessions. I expected Myles Gabite to do more than he had in the teams’ first game. His 175 rushing yards were only part of the correction. FLOAT SZN added 157 receiving yards, and Watzon took only one sack after taking four against Petalburg. The key I’d carry forward is Mossdeep’s ability to finish with different receivers. The revised expectation is that the Eclipse may need to use all of them.

Three shorter touchdowns against Sunyshore give Mossdeep a useful starting point. Ninjaskamara ran left for one yard on fourth-and-one, then caught an eight-yard pass late in the second quarter. Gronkaludon caught a 14-yard touchdown on third-and-eight early in the fourth. The run gave Mossdeep a way to win from a yard out after an incomplete pass on third down. The catches gave Marino two different scoring options in a part of the field where a longer route has less room to develop.

Marino completed 20 of 33 passes for 313 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. BeckhmJr had five catches for 146 yards and two scores, including the 70-yard winner. Gronkaludon caught all three targets. Ninjaskamara and Shawn Mareman added five catches between them. Saffron’s front has a strong incentive to make him spend the afternoon looking at second-and-long. For a checkable Mossdeep key, count how many trips inside the Saffron 20 end in a touchdown. A first half that ends with two field goals from at least 40 yards suits the Psi Corps.

Mossdeep led the league with 2,551 regular-season rushing yards. Saffron allowed a league-low 694. The first meeting produced 96 rushing yards on 20 Eclipse carries. That’s enough to keep using the run, and it makes the next call after a short gain especially important. A first-down carry that gets four near the 20 leaves Marino and his back six yards to find on the next two downs. A carry that stalls at the line asks a receiver to do the harder part in a tighter space.

Saffron can remember where those kicks came from. Chen Norton Jr had four sacks in Week 10. NeMarcus Tare had four last week, part of a six-sack performance in which Mt. Silver lost 33 yards. A sack on first or second down can force another long throw before the offense reaches a comfortable finish, and a sack on third down can make a once-reasonable kick substantially longer. Mossdeep gained only 85 rushing yards against Sunyshore, but Ninjaskamara averaged 5.5 on eleven carries. The run remains an option around scoring range when Marino gets a defense that is particularly eager to play the next pass.
How Saffron can finish against Mossdeep

Saffron won at Mt. Silver after producing touchdown drives from several starting positions. The two early drives covered 64 and 93 yards and ended with throws to Gengar Pickens for eleven and eight. Archam Manning later found Dam Skattebo from the one and Woobat from 17. Skattebo’s late rushing touchdown came after the defense took over the ball on downs in Reds territory. Those were two distinct problems for Mt. Silver: defending an offense driving the length of the field and keeping a short field from becoming another seven points.

Manning didn’t take a sack in that game and threw four touchdowns with no interceptions. His decision on fourth-and-seven is a good reminder of how Saffron can build a short finish. He missed HeeDee Lamb on the previous two throws, found Skattebo short right for 21, then came right back to Lamb for the 16-yard catch that set up Woobat. Saffron was 3-for-9 on third down, so that one fourth-down conversion changed the opportunities the offense could use. In this matchup I want to count sacks allowed alongside those short scoring chances. If Manning is still getting off clean throws on second and third down in the fourth quarter, his receivers can give Saffron a winning drive in several ways.

The Eclipse have just allowed three rushing touchdowns. Sunyshore converted fourth-and-one on Gabite’s 16-yard touchdown, and Kobra Khan got eight up the middle for the last score. The Psi Corps can test that area with Skattebo and still threaten the secondary from the same spot. Marshall Flock has one week remaining and will miss the final. Poury Holt has three weeks, as does Saffron fullback Emmitt Smoth. Joey Sporeter and Lamb have new minor entries that list zero weeks. Saffron’s receiving choices matter more if Mossdeep spends an extra defender on a back who can score from the one.
Watch who has to finish from farther out

The first meeting offers a good benchmark for each offense. Saffron’s two touchdown drives of the first half went 80 and 75 yards. Its field goal followed another drive of 70. The offense created all of those chances from deep in its own territory, then went scoreless in the second half. Mossdeep’s winning drive started from its 20 and saw Marino complete all four of his throws, with four carries by Ninjaskamara between the third completion and the touchdown. Those are demanding drives to repeat. Both offenses can raise their odds of finishing by shortening the field with a return or by forcing a punt before the opponent crosses midfield.

That’s one reason a game can look different from the yardage total. Saffron outgained Mossdeep 334–314 and lost the first meeting. Sunyshore outgained Mossdeep 469–398 and lost last week. One of Mossdeep’s scoring drives against Sunyshore needed only 19 yards after Derrat Brooks’s interception. The Eclipse had to play nearly the length of the field on other touchdown drives. Give a finalist a possession 19 yards away, and the matchup in scoring range becomes the whole possession. Give it a full field four times and the opposing defense has four chances to spoil a series before it needs to defend the goal line.
Score pick

I had Mossdeep 31–24 in my opening bracket. The finalists are the ones I expected, and the latest conference games give Saffron a better scoring case than I allowed at the time. The Psi Corps answered a difficult second half at Mt. Silver with three touchdowns, two through the air and one on the ground. Manning has thrown eight touchdown passes in two rounds. Mossdeep’s response against Sunyshore was just as instructive. The Eclipse scored with manageable downs, from third-and-eight and in one snap from their own 30.

My pick is Mossdeep 31, Saffron 26. I expect Saffron’s rush to force the Eclipse to kick at least once, and I expect Manning to put enough receivers in play to keep the game within one possession. The narrow edge is Mossdeep’s ability to turn one more visit into a touchdown through Ninjaskamara or Gronkaludon. That’s the difference I’ll be looking for on the first trip either team makes inside the 20.

matchups.title: Who finishes more drives inside the 20?
matchups.analysis: Mossdeep won the Week 10 meeting 20–17. At the neutral-site Indigo Bowl, Saffron brings 13 sacks over two games and Mossdeep brings five touchdowns scored against Sunyshore.
matchups.matchup: Finishing drives against two productive pass rushes
matchups.awayKey: Track touchdowns on trips inside the Saffron 20. Gronkaludon and Ninjaskamara can give Marino quick finishing options.
matchups.homeKey: Keep Manning upright on second and third down. Skattebo’s receiving threat can move the chains when the first down gets away.

prediction.reason: Mossdeep has finished recent scoring drives through a tight end, a back and an outside receiver. I give the Eclipse a small edge to turn one more promising possession into a touchdown.

articles.author: ellis-quill
articles.title: Marino and BeckhmJr answer in one play to send Mossdeep to the Indigo Bowl
articles.dek: A 70-yard touchdown in the final minute rescues the Eclipse after Sunyshore takes the lead; Mossdeep wins 37–31 and reaches the final at 19–0.

body.text: Mossdeep had forty-four seconds on the clock, seventy yards to cover and an unbeaten season that had just become somebody else's lead. Dram Marino threw deep right to Accel BeckhmJr. The play carried all the way to the end zone. By the time Adam Vinathorn added the extra point, the Eclipse had turned a 31–30 deficit into a 37–31 lead, and Sunyshore had thirty-five seconds to find another answer.

The Starseekers nearly spent every one of them productively. DeZhaun Watzon completed passes to Kobra Khan, FLOAT SZN, Myles Gabite and BJ Vickers, then spiked the ball with three seconds remaining. His last throw, snapped at 0:02, reached FLOAT SZN for nine yards. Will Shells made the tackle. Mossdeep's nineteenth win was secure, and the Indigo Bowl would pair the Eclipse with Saffron.

There are comfortable ways to reach a championship game. This one required Mossdeep to keep responding after Sunyshore repeatedly demonstrated why it belonged there. Gabite rushed for 175 yards and two touchdowns. FLOAT SZN caught seven passes for 157. The visitors gained 469 total yards to the Eclipse's 398, collected twenty first downs to fourteen and led during the final minute. Their season ended because Marino and BeckhmJr needed only one snap to change the lead again.

Marino finished 20 of 33 for 313 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. BeckhmJr caught five balls for 146 yards and two scores. Those totals include the decisive seventy yards, but the receiver had already supplied a second-quarter touchdown and a thirty-eight-yard gain on an earlier scoring drive. Mossdeep's most dramatic completion grew from a partnership that had been consequential throughout the game.
Sunyshore establishes its offense

Karson Jones's team opened with a seven-play, seventy-five-yard touchdown drive. Watzon found FLOAT SZN deep right for twenty-nine, Gabite ran right for twenty-three and the Starseekers kept moving toward the goal line. Gabite finished with an eight-yard run up the middle at the 4:17 snap. Sunyshore had arrived with more than an intention to keep the score respectable.

Mossdeep's first possession took twelve plays and nearly three minutes. Ninjaskamara ran for eight after an opening incompletion, Gronkaludon converted third-and-two and Marino spread short throws among several targets. Shawn Mareman contributed a sixteen-yard run. At the goal line, Lorenzo Steel's five-yard catch left the Eclipse close enough to consider running on fourth down. After Marino's third-down throw to Steel fell incomplete, Ninjaskamara scored from one yard out on fourth-and-one, and Vinathorn tied it with the kick.

Sunyshore answered with a field goal before the first quarter ended. Gabite opened that possession with eleven yards, and Watzon hit Fera LaGatr for twenty-five. Mossdeep then forced two incompletions after stopping Gabite for a loss. Kayden Lyons made the thirty-three-yard kick at 0:03. That sequence mattered because a productive Starseekers drive still ended short of the end zone; such small differences would remain visible all evening.

Ninjaskamara supplied three consecutive productive carries to start Mossdeep's next scoring possession. Marino then converted third-and-ten with a deep-right completion to Gronkaludon and went back to that side for BeckhmJr's twenty-four-yard touchdown. The Eclipse led 14–10. They had shown both ways to advance: a long opening possession assembled from several contributors and a later drive finished by consecutive downfield throws.

Sunyshore kept using Gabite. He ran for nine, twenty-three, eleven, three and seven yards on the next possession, forcing Mossdeep to spend snap after snap dealing with the ground game. Watzon eventually found MF STOMP for a ten-yard touchdown on third-and-ten at the two-minute warning. The Starseekers were ahead again, 17–14, and their ability to finish that drive made the earlier rushing work count.
Brooks gives Mossdeep a short field

The Eclipse's next possession ended after Marino took a third-down sack. Sunyshore had a chance to carry its lead into halftime and perhaps add to it. Instead, Derrat Brooks intercepted Watzon's deep-right throw on the 1:06 snap and returned it twenty-two yards. Mossdeep began its next drive with only nineteen yards remaining to the end zone.

Ninjaskamara ran for eleven, then caught Marino's short-left pass for an eight-yard touchdown. The extra point was missed, leaving Mossdeep ahead 20–17. Brooks's interception was the only thrown interception of the game. It changed the available field as much as it changed possession, giving an offense that had just punted an immediate opportunity to score.

body.alt: Stadium lights shine over an empty Mossdeep football field viewed from the sideline at dusk.
body.caption: An imagined halftime view from the Mossdeep sideline.

body.text: Brooks finished with two tackles, two passes defended and that interception, earning the game's defensive award. He did not need a large tackle total to make the most influential defensive play before halftime. Ninjaskamara's two touchdowns also came through different jobs: the fourth-down rush in the first quarter and the receiving finish after the turnover. His final offensive line was sixty rushing yards and ten receiving yards.

The third quarter supplied a pause in the scoring without much comfort for either sideline. Mossdeep punted on its first three possessions after halftime. Druddamukong sacked Watzon on Sunyshore's first offensive snap of the half, helping force a punt. The Starseekers later advanced fifty-three yards on a drive that ended in a missed field goal. Neither side scored in the period.

For Michael Dorrill, the three consecutive punts will survive the celebration. So will the rushing lanes Gabite kept finding. Mossdeep had finished the regular season allowing 130 points across seventeen games and had beaten Dewford 40–3 in the divisional round. Sunyshore asked much harder questions than those recent numbers might have encouraged anyone to expect. The Eclipse had to win with the game they were actually playing.
The fourth-quarter finish

Mossdeep's next drive began late in the third quarter and crossed into the fourth. Ninjulio Jones converted third-and-seven with an eleven-yard catch. Steel gained fourteen to open the final period, BeckhmJr followed with thirty-eight, and Marino eventually found Gronkaludon for the touchdown on third-and-eight. Vinathorn's kick made it 27–17 with just under five minutes left.

Three straight punts in the third quarter. A hundred eighty-two rushing yards allowed. We've got plenty to review. The offense answered when it had to. Now we've got to prepare so the next game doesn't require that answer.
body.speaker: Michael Dorrill

body.text: Sunyshore needed only forty-two seconds of drive time to respond. FLOAT SZN opened with a thirty-three-yard reception, MF STOMP added sixteen and Khan caught a third-down pass that kept the offense close enough to go for it. Gabite then ran up the middle for sixteen yards on fourth-and-one. The visitors were back within three. That decision produced a touchdown when a failed attempt would have left Mossdeep ahead by ten with possession.

Vinathorn gave the Eclipse a different sort of margin at the end of their next drive. Mossdeep reached a long field-goal attempt after an incompletion on third down. The Maractus made it from fifty-eight yards on the 1:55 snap, extending the lead to 30–24. His kicking line would contain one made field goal from one attempt, and its distance explained why Sunyshore still needed a touchdown.

body.alt: A football sails between the uprights with Maractus No. 96 in the distance.
body.caption: Adam Vinathorn’s 58-yard field goal extended Mossdeep’s fourth-quarter lead to 30–24.

body.text: Watzon immediately leaned on FLOAT SZN. Three consecutive completions gained fourteen, seventeen and twenty-six yards. Gabite ran for eight, lost two and then caught a five-yard pass on third-and-four. Khan finished the drive with an eight-yard run up the middle at 0:51. Lyons's extra point, logged at 0:48, gave Sunyshore the 31–30 lead.

Ninjaskamara returned the kickoff twenty-eight yards to the Mossdeep thirty. Marino and BeckhmJr then delivered the seventy-yard touchdown on the first offensive snap. The Eclipse had spent a full evening answering Sunyshore's sustained drives; this answer took one completion. It also left enough time for the Starseekers' final advance, which is why Shells's tackle on the last catch belongs in the same ending as the touchdown.

Mossdeep advances with work for its defense and proof of what its passing game can rescue. Sunyshore leaves with a loss that should be described at its actual scale: a conference finalist that led the unbeaten favorite in the final minute and made it produce an exceptional response. The Eclipse will face Saffron with the perfect record intact. Keeping it intact for one more game will require another complete answer.

articles.author: mara-voss
articles.title: Saffron converts fourth-and-seven, then closes the door on Mt. Silver
articles.dek: Archam Manning throws four touchdowns, Dam Skattebo supplies the late answers and six sacks help the Psi Corps win the conference final 38–27.

body.text: Saffron faced fourth-and-seven with less than two minutes remaining and Mt. Silver ahead 27–21. Archam Manning had just missed HeeDee Lamb deep right on third down. On the next snap, logged at 1:54, he threw short right to Dam Skattebo. The completion gained twenty-one yards. Three plays after the failed third-down throw, Manning had found Woobat for a seventeen-yard touchdown, and the Psi Corps were an extra point from taking back the lead.

That conversion was the most urgent offensive answer in a 38–27 Saffron victory. What followed made the margin: Ariados stopped Garshawn Lynch short on fourth-and-two, Skattebo scored on Saffron's very next offensive play, and Chen Norton Jr. ended Mt. Silver's following possession with a fourth-down sack. A one-point game became a two-score result because the Psi Corps won consecutive late situations on both sides of the ball.

Saffron advances to face Mossdeep in the Indigo Bowl. Manning finished 18 of 28 for 254 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Skattebo supplied eighty-seven rushing yards, thirty-seven receiving yards and a touchdown in each phase. NeMarcus Tare recorded four sacks, with Norton adding two. The offensive and defensive numbers describe the contributors; the timing explains why their team survived.

Mt. Silver had led twice in the second half after falling behind 14–0. Tauros Woodson's punt returns were central to that reversal. Jacoby Brizzet threw two touchdowns after taking over the passing work from Crem Ftzpatrik, who left the game with a ten-week injury entry. The Reds had enough production to make Saffron chase the lead. Their final two offensive possessions gave them eight snaps and no first downs.
Manning scores on his first two possessions

Saffron's opening touchdown drive used Skattebo immediately. Manning hit him short left for fifteen yards, and the Darmanitan followed with runs of thirteen and eight. Mothel Irving caught a seventeen-yard pass before Gengar Pickens finished the drive with an eleven-yard touchdown reception. The offense covered sixty-four yards in five plays and gave Trent Scarboro an early lead without needing a third-down rescue.

The second touchdown possession was even more direct. Starting with ninety-three yards to travel, Manning completed five consecutive passes. Bysson Witten gained twenty-nine, Lamb twenty-six, Pickens thirteen and Mothel eighteen. Manning then went back to Pickens for the eight-yard score. Four receivers touched the ball on a drive composed entirely of completions, with every snap beginning on first down.

Pickens finished with three catches for thirty-two yards and two touchdowns. His whole receiving line came from those opening possessions. That is a useful distinction when looking at the offense: the player who finished its early drives was different from the player who supplied its most important late conversion. Manning kept finding productive targets without needing one receiver to accumulate the entire afternoon.

body.alt: A view across a mountain football stadium with red and silver seating and a pink and cyan visiting section.
body.caption: An imagined view of the conference championship at Mt. Silver. Gengar Pickens caught two first-quarter touchdowns.

body.text: Mt. Silver's first three possessions ended in punts. Norton sacked Crem on third-and-eight in the first quarter. Tare reached him again early in the second. Crem's last named play in the passing sequence was that sack at 5:40; Brizzet's first named pass came at 5:01. The report lists Crem's ten-week injury but does not identify an injury timestamp or establish which play caused it. Assigning the injury to either sack would go beyond what the game records show.

Brizzet eventually helped the Reds finish a ten-play, fifty-eight-yard touchdown drive. He took a sack from Tare along the way, but Mt. Silver kept the possession alive and reached Doduo for a six-yard score at the 1:56 snap. The extra point missed. Saffron carried a 14–6 lead to halftime after its own offense had slowed, and the Reds had a reason to believe the opening deficit was manageable.
Woodson changes the field

The second half began with a mistake Saffron could afford only because its defense held up. Manning returned the kickoff twenty-three yards and fumbled; Mt. Silver's Scizor recovered. The Reds gained an immediate scoring chance but failed to turn it into points, ending the possession with a missed thirty-six-yard field goal. The takeaway and the subsequent missed kick need to be kept together when describing the shift in momentum.

Woodson then did more to change the game than that turnover had. After Saffron punted, the Tauros returned the ball sixty-six yards, setting up the Reds with a short field. Lynch scored on a fourteen-yard run to the right, and the extra point cut the deficit to 14–13. Saffron's defense was repeatedly being asked to protect very different amounts of field from the long drives its offense had enjoyed early.

On the next Saffron punt, Woodson took the return seventy-nine yards for a touchdown. Mt. Silver led 20–14 after the kick. The Reds had scored fourteen third-quarter points without needing Brizzet to throw a touchdown pass in the period. Their return game had supplied the short field for one score and the entire distance for the other.

Woodson's official line credits four punt returns for 157 yards and a touchdown. The two spectacular returns explain why Saffron's advantage in passing efficiency was insufficient to control the score. Field position and a special-teams touchdown had changed the terms. Scarboro's offense now needed a full response after beginning the second half with a fumble and punts.
You give up those returns and everybody feels it. Then you still have to go play. Our guys kept giving each other another chance, and when fourth down came, they made that chance count.
body.speaker: Trent Scarboro

body.text: Manning produced it on a seventy-eight-yard drive. Saffron worked back down the field and finished with a one-yard short-left touchdown pass to Skattebo at the 0:42 snap. The extra point restored the lead, 21–20. Skattebo had already helped establish the opening possession; now he supplied the finish that allowed the Psi Corps to leave the third quarter ahead despite Woodson's returns.
Mt. Silver retakes the lead

The Reds' next scoring drive lasted into the fourth quarter. Brizzet and Lynch kept it moving, and even another sack from Tare could not stop it. Tare dropped Brizzet for six yards on first-and-five at 3:16. On the next snap, Brizzet found Doduo deep right for an eleven-yard touchdown. Mt. Silver led 27–21 after the extra point, with under three minutes remaining.

Brizzet's response to that sack deserves its own place in the loss. He finished 18 of 30 for 180 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He absorbed four sacks, while Crem had taken two. The quarterback change did not prevent the Reds from threatening through the air, and Doduo supplied both passing touchdowns. Lynch added ninety-four rushing yards and sixty-four receiving yards, giving Brizzet another productive outlet.

Saffron's next possession reached the two-minute warning facing third-and-seven. Manning's incomplete deep-right pass to Lamb left fourth down. The earlier touchdowns, the four sacks from Tare and the regular-season record could not convert it for him. He went short right to Skattebo, who gained twenty-one and kept the season moving. Manning then found Lamb for sixteen before going deep left to Woobat for the seventeen-yard touchdown.

The extra point put Saffron ahead 28–27 at 1:28. Mt. Silver had the ball and time to respond. Brizzet opened with two incompletions, then found Prinplup for eight yards on third-and-ten. On fourth-and-two, the Reds handed to Lynch up the middle. Ariados made the tackle after one yard. Saffron took possession, and Skattebo immediately ran up the middle for a touchdown on the next snap.

body.alt: Darmanitan No. 22 carries the football up the middle toward the end zone.
body.caption: Dam Skattebo’s late touchdown run extended Saffron’s lead after a fourth-down stop.

body.text: Norton's fourth-down sack ended the Reds' next chance. Saffron ran the clock down and added Octillery's thirty-one-yard field goal with five seconds showing before the snap. The Psi Corps had scored seventeen fourth-quarter points and finished with a 38–27 win. Their closing sequence combined a passing conversion, a receiving touchdown, a run stop, a rushing touchdown and a sack. Every part was needed before the score looked comfortable.

The Bowl opponent will test the protection and coverage more severely. Mossdeep just survived Sunyshore through Marino's four-touchdown game, including the seventy-yard winner. Saffron's six sacks against Mt. Silver are an encouraging result, while its return coverage and Manning's lost fumble remain concrete corrections. Scarboro has a championship finalist because his team answered those problems within the game. It now has one week to make fewer of them against the Eclipse.

art.alt: Saffron’s Ninetales No. 42 pauses on a stairway overlooking the field.

articles.author: mara-voss
articles.title: Mossdeep can keep Saffron's rush away from Dram Marino
articles.dek: The Eclipse have already won one difficult game against the Psi Corps. Earlier answers for the pass rush and tighter tackling can make the rematch easier.

body.text: I want Lorenzo Steel in Mossdeep’s first passing series. I want Gronkaludon in the progression before the chains get long and Ninjaskamara catching passes while Saffron still has to respect his carries. The glamorous part of this championship is Accel BeckhmJr running deep. The part I’m watching first is whether Dram Marino can get the ball somewhere useful before Chen Norton Jr gets to him.

Week 10 explains my impatience. Norton, the Medicham who wears No. 56 for the Psi Corps, took Marino down four times in Mossdeep’s 20–17 win. Two of the sacks came on consecutive plays after Ninjulio Jones’ 44-yard kickoff return. The Eclipse started in position to make a quick answer near halftime. They wound up asking Gronkaludon for 18 yards on third-and-22 so Adam Vinathorn could try a 47-yard field goal. He hit it off the upright. That’s a terrific kick and a dreadful way to spend a good return.

Norton’s fourth sack came on third-and-seven after halftime. Marino finished without an interception, and I credit him for keeping the ball. The standard for a championship offense has to include keeping the downs manageable, too. Saffron has recorded thirteen sacks in its past two games, with nine from NeMarcus Tare and four from Norton. Tare dropped Jacoby Brizzet on second-and-five in the first half, and Norton ended the Reds’ final drive on fourth-and-six. I’d rather have Marino getting the ball to a receiver who can turn second-and-seven into a first down than asking him to erase a sack after one of those two has already collected it.
The throws that buy the next call

The last 80 yards of the first meeting tell me how Michael Dorrill can make that rush work harder. Marino took over at his 20 with 1:48 left, trailing by four. He threw short right to Ninjaskamara for seven, then deep left to him for 19. BeckhmJr gained 22 deep right. Ninjaskamara made four consecutive runs for 26 yards, and Marino finished from the six with a short-right touchdown pass to BeckhmJr. The winning touchdown came on the snap logged at 0:49. It had used both edges, a back as a receiver and as a runner, and the lead receiver at two different depths.

Marino had a version of that available against Sunyshore. He took a seven-yard sack on third-and-one in the second quarter, a down where the Eclipse had earned the right to ask a simpler question. After halftime their first three possessions ended in punts and gained 14 yards combined. A five-yard catch on third-and-six and a deep incompletion on third-and-nine left the same unit walking off. Later Ninjulio caught an 11-yard throw short middle on third-and-seven late in the third. Steel caught the next pass short right for 14. Two different bodies to tackle and two different areas of the field had Sunyshore dealing with first down again.

Gronkaludon ended that 81-yard drive with a 14-yard catch deep right on third-and-eight. I’d love to get him a few of the earlier throws, too. He had already gained seven on third-and-two in the opening quarter and moved the chains on a deep throw on third-and-ten in the second. A tight end who moves the chains on both downs can make the protection’s day easier well before he helps bail it out. Steel had three catches for 33 yards, including another 14-yard gain short right on third-and-eight in the fourth. Marino has actual completions to draw on across the field.
A third-and-eight conversion earns a first down. It also earns a question about how we got to third-and-eight. We can handle both in the same meeting.
body.speaker: Michael Dorrill

body.text: A short throw gives Saffron a chance to win with the tackle, and a back asked to help with pressure is one fewer immediate outlet. I’d vary where the help comes from and get the ball to a target who’s already threatening the sticks. On the opening drive against Sunyshore, Shawn Mareman’s nine-yard catch on second-and-seven moved them, and Damien Woodo’s 15-yard catch on second-and-two kept them moving. If the Psi Corps have to defend that variety, Marino can choose a down to ask BeckhmJr for 25 and keep the opportunity to run the ball when the look suits Ninjaskamara. That gives the receiver who just went 70 for the winning touchdown a cleaner chance to get there again.
Mossdeep’s defense needs the tackle after the throw

Trent Scarboro has his own evidence for making a defense cover the whole field. Late against Mt. Silver, Archam Manning missed HeeDee Lamb twice to the deep right, including a third-and-seven breakup. With 1:54 left he threw short right to Dam Skattebo for 21 on fourth-and-seven. Twelve seconds later Lamb caught a short-left pass for 16. Woobat took the next pass, deep left, for the 17-yard go-ahead touchdown. Three players gave Manning three gains. The Reds had already broken up the third-down throw, and they still had to tackle Skattebo before he made the next seven yards.

That first conversion deserves Mossdeep’s attention. Sunyshore began its last touchdown drive with FLOAT SZN catches of 14, 17 and 26 yards, using short right, deep left and deep right. The Eclipse had just gone up 30–24 on Vinathorn’s 58-yard field goal. Sunyshore gained 57 yards on its first three throws before the ground game got the chance to finish. Skattebo is a different player, but Manning’s fourth-and-seven gave him a short catch with room to turn it into a large gain. I’d make finding the back a priority when the apparent passing down draws attention to the outside receiver.

The Eclipse had a model for this in the first meeting. Saffron recovered a Mossdeep fumble, and Shawn Mareman sacked Manning near the end of the third quarter. Ray Glewis stopped Skattebo for a three-yard loss to start the fourth. Druddamukong took Manning down on third-and-eighteen. Those three plays turned a change of possession into a punt without requiring a defensive takeaway. I’d take that sequence into the last five minutes of the Bowl. If the play is there to put Manning behind the sticks, finish the series while he’s still there.

Marshall Flock’s one-week listing keeps the corner out of the Bowl. Back Poury Holt has three weeks remaining. Joey Sporeter has a minor entry at zero weeks, as does Lamb on the other side, and Saffron fullback Emmitt Smoth has three weeks. Mossdeep ought to prepare to see Lamb and Skattebo on the same passing down. If Manning has the time he had against Mt. Silver, where he took zero sacks on 28 attempts, the defenders closing on the first catch have to preserve the down they’ve earned.

I’ll take Mossdeep 34, Saffron 28. I expect Tare and Norton to wreck a possession, and Manning has the throws to collect on it. Marino can keep the next drive from looking like the first. On an early third down with a few yards to go, I’m looking for No. 24 or No. 67 to catch one before the pressure reaches him. The Eclipse can earn the deep ball on their own timetable this time.

art.alt: Drampa No. 12 studies gold arrows drawn over a football field.

articles.author: ellis-quill
articles.title: Mossdeep’s last game at 19–0
articles.dek: Michael Dorrill has spent a season demanding the next good possession. The undefeated Eclipse need one more game’s worth of them.

body.text: Dram Marino had 44 seconds, 70 yards and a one-point deficit. I asked him about the moment the conference championship came down to that accounting. He talked about the kickoff. Ninjaskamara returned it 28 yards to the Mossdeep 30, where Marino started the possession that ended with Accel BeckhmJr in the end zone.
It gives you a yard line and a clock. Those are two things I can do something with.
body.speaker: Dram Marino

body.text: I wanted him to tell me how an unbeaten season felt in his chest. He gave me two numbers he could use. That answer is worth remembering when Mossdeep takes the field against Saffron. The Eclipse won all seventeen regular-season games, took their bye and beat Dewford and Sunyshore. Nineteen wins give a team an increasingly peculiar job. A good performance preserves a condition everyone has begun to expect. A bad ending becomes the first thing someone brings up about all of it. Mossdeep has kept answering immediate and ordinary questions as the stakes have become harder to describe.
What the coach counts

Michael Dorrill’s team won its nineteenth game. He came away with a problem that lasted most of the third quarter. He had four Mossdeep punts to discuss after the conference championship, three of them in a third quarter when a lead of 20–17 might change hands on anybody’s next possession. The three drives gained a combined 14 yards. The winning throw makes the arithmetic easier to bear. I asked whether it made the third-quarter tape easier to watch.

It saved the game. I still have to watch the third quarter. If we’re asking the defense to keep taking the field with three points to work with, the offense owes them a better reason than “we’ll get the next one.”
body.speaker: Michael Dorrill

body.text: The defense did take the field again. Sunyshore finished the third quarter with the same 17 points it had at halftime. Mossdeep scored early in the fourth when Gronkaludon caught the 14-yard pass that completed an 81-yard drive. Then the teams went through the whole business again. At 1:55, Adam Vinathorn hit a 58-yard field goal for a 30–24 lead. Kobra Khan scored with 51 seconds left, and the kick put Sunyshore up 31–30. Vinathorn had supplied an excellent answer to a question that lasted a little over a minute.

Dorrill’s team scored 724 points in the regular season. Most weeks the final score gave him more room to discuss what needed work. The conference championship gave him little such room. A linebacker fielded the consequences of a failed offensive possession. A kick returner gave the quarterback the 30 instead of something worse. A tight end made three catches as the two principal scoring threats drew plenty of attention. The championship asks a team accustomed to room for error to do another full afternoon’s work together.

Dewford saw how it works when the offense gets going early. Three Mossdeep drives at the start of the divisional game traveled 74, 66 and 83 yards. All ended in touchdowns, and the Eclipse won 40–3. Sunyshore forced Mossdeep to come from behind four times. A player can spend a season on a club that scores like the Eclipse and get very few chances to learn how his teammates sound when they need him to solve a problem right then. The conference game gave them all a long afternoon to get acquainted.
A teammate can give you back a possession

Mossdeep was behind 17–14 late in the first half against Sunyshore when its offense punted after Marino took a sack on third-and-one. DeZhaun Watzon threw deep right with 1:06 left. Derrat Brooks intercepted and returned it 22 yards. Nineteen yards and two plays later, Marino threw short left to Ninjaskamara for a touchdown with 40 seconds left. The missed extra point kept it 20–17, which is precisely the kind of punctuation that keeps a good result from feeling as tidy as the account of it.

I’d put that touchdown next to the 70-yarder. The return gave Marino and his teammates the easiest field they saw all game. A running back caught the pass that made the defensive work count. After watching three punts in the third quarter, the defense still owed the offense its best chance to answer. None of that makes the Eclipse immune to an opponent getting ahead with 48 seconds on the clock. It gives their players something recognizable to do if it happens.

Saffron’s case for winning the Bowl begins with having people who understand the same obligations. Archam Manning lost a fumble on the opening kickoff of the second half against Mt. Silver. The Reds missed a 36-yard field goal after recovering it. Tauros Woodson later returned a punt 66 yards to set up Garshawn Lynch’s touchdown. Woodson returned Saffron’s next punt 79 yards for another touchdown, and the Psi Corps trailed 20–14. Manning went back to work and found Dam Skattebo from the one for the score that brought the lead back. Later, after two throws to HeeDee Lamb fell incomplete, the offense kept the ball on fourth-and-seven and found enough from Skattebo, Lamb and Woobat to go in front again. That could easily be the other side’s version of the week we just watched.
The Bowl asks for another familiar job

Marshall Flock still has a week left on his injury listing. Back Poury Holt and Saffron fullback Emmitt Smoth each have three. The Eclipse have already played a close playoff game without Flock, and Sunyshore still gained 287 passing yards. The secondary will have to cover Manning’s short throws with that same absence. Lamb and Joey Sporeter each have a minor entry at zero weeks. Defending the next catch is the assignment whoever is in, and covering the next down after Skattebo gets loose might be the one that decides it.

Saffron lost 20–17 in their first meeting. It had led 17–6 at halftime. BeckhmJr’s winner on the snap logged at 0:49 and Electric Berry’s interception on Manning’s first response proved Mossdeep could finish that afternoon. Then the Psi Corps lost by three to Mt. Silver, too, and earned one of those rematches back just last week. Manning threw four touchdown passes in that win. The second rematch gives him a chance to give the campaign an entirely different ending.

I put Mossdeep over Cinnabar in my opening bracket. The Eclipse still get my pick, with a closer finish against the opponent they’ll actually face. Call it Mossdeep 30, Saffron 27. I can picture a second-and-six catch by Gronkaludon giving Vinathorn a shorter attempt than the 58-yarder he just had to hit, or a downfield tackle that keeps Manning from getting another set of downs. I expect the Eclipse to get one more of those familiar jobs done. Dorrill has had reasons to put the first nineteen games back on the screen. He can decide what the twentieth buys him after the kick.

art.alt: Magenta-and-gold warmup towels hang beside a closed door overlooking an empty football stadium.

articles.author: dorian-pike
articles.title: Saffron should put the Indigo Bowl in Dam Skattebo’s hands
articles.dek: Mossdeep spent its conference championship trying to get off the field against two productive backs. Saffron can put both jobs in the hands of No. 22.

body.text: I spent last week urging Karson Jones to let Myles Gabite decide how long Dram Marino had to wait for the ball. Gabite rushed for 175 yards and two touchdowns. Sunyshore had the lead with 48 seconds left. My pick was still Mossdeep, and the winning touchdown came on the next snap from scrimmage. Karson got almost everything his rushing game could reasonably give him. In the Indigo Bowl, I’m taking the team with a back who can claim the next first down on a handoff or on a throw. Dam Skattebo ought to get enough of both to make it count.

Mossdeep is 19–0, and the number deserves its own line on the standings. Here are three more numbers that deserve Trent Scarboro’s attention. Sunyshore ran for 182 yards. FLOAT SZN caught seven passes for 157 yards. The possession that put the Starseekers in front began on their own 23 and took 59 seconds to reach the end zone. Mossdeep’s offense had just spent more than two minutes driving into position for a 58-yard field goal. Its defense put the offense right back to work.

Skattebo gives Saffron a chance to combine the jobs Gabite and FLOAT SZN shared. He rushed for 1,026 yards and 18 touchdowns in the regular season. His 20 catches added 221 yards and three touchdowns. Against Mt. Silver, he took thirteen carries for 87 yards and caught all three passes Manning sent him for 37 more. Two of his sixteen touches ended in the end zone. I’d make the Eclipse deal with him on more than sixteen snaps if they give Saffron a competitive score and a reason to keep going.
Make the run earn its place

Gabite is an excellent piece of evidence, and Dewford is the one I’d bring up in the meeting immediately afterward. The Breakers had 30 rushing yards in a 40–3 loss. Excadrill finished with 27 on ten carries. An offense chasing a three-touchdown start can run itself into an impressive shortage of time. If the first few carries for Skattebo buy third-and-seven, Scarboro has to let Manning play football. The point of a heavier workload is to earn first downs and spend a little of the resulting time, which the back will be happy to do in that order.

Skattebo ran for 13 up the middle and eight to the right on successive first downs on Saffron’s opening drive against Mt. Silver. Manning had started that drive by throwing to him for 15. The drive before Saffron’s third touchdown offered a different version of the same arrangement. With Saffron down 20–14, Skattebo ran up the middle for 15 and then for seven on first-and-eight. Manning finished the job with the short throw to him from the one. Mt. Silver had good reason to defend the run on second-and-one. It had good reason to watch the same player after the ball left Manning’s hand.

Saffron will play without Emmitt Smoth, listed at three weeks, so count the work of the available backfield. Pawmo contributed seven rushing yards on three carries last week. HeeDee Lamb, whose minor listing shows zero weeks, already has a season’s worth of catching and rushing production from the slot. If Mossdeep goes after Skattebo aggressively on early downs, Manning has someone ready to make it expensive. At the other end, Marshall Flock still has one week left, Poury Holt has three and Joey Sporeter has a zero-week minor entry. The injury that opens the most obvious receiving question is the corner’s absence. Get Skattebo a catch with space and every defender still has to arrive on time.
The throw that keeps it Skattebo’s game

There’s precedent for the catch in this matchup. On Saffron’s first touchdown drive in Week 10, Manning threw deep left to Skattebo for 24 on third-and-seven. Pickens followed with the next conversion and scored one play later. That afternoon already showed the Eclipse what can happen when the player they have to account for near the handoff gets downfield on a long passing down. Scarboro has two different depths to call for when seven yards are required. I’d bring both to the Bowl.

The play I’m buying comes after Saffron’s running game had ceased to be the immediate concern. The Psi Corps were down 27–21, and Manning had tried Lamb deep right on consecutive downs. With 1:54 left, they faced fourth-and-seven. Skattebo caught the ball short right and gained 21. That is the full price of the catch for Mt. Silver. Fourteen of those yards took Saffron beyond the line it had to get. Lamb caught the next throw for 16, and Woobat finished with a 17-yard score. The back turned the last available down into an opportunity for two receivers to do their best work.
Seven was enough for the down. I knew the guys would be ready if I could get us another one.
body.speaker: Dam Skattebo

body.text: I’d treat that pass like an option while the game is still comfortably young. With the front charging upfield after Manning and the secondary watching Lamb or Pickens, a pass to the back can put the ball beyond the first group of defenders. If the Eclipse keep it to five on fourth-and-seven, I’ll credit them and accept the consequences for my pick. I’d enjoy seeing them prove it against the player who just made the Reds try to tackle him 21 yards after the snap.
Finish the drive with the lead

Week 10 showed the cost of leaving the game with Marino. Saffron led 17–6 at halftime, went scoreless after it and gave up the winning 80-yard drive after punting to a touchback. Marino used Ninjaskamara on two passes and four consecutive carries on that drive. He had to spend time and yards reaching the finish. Last week, all he needed on the last drive was one throw. If Saffron can get in front in the fourth quarter, another first down for Skattebo is a more attractive way to control the remaining minute than giving Marino another opportunity to decide how valuable it is.

Mossdeep can break my forecast by taking an early lead and forcing Saffron to discard any timetable. Ninjaskamara had five touchdowns against Dewford, and Marino has thrown for seven in two playoff games without an interception. I can add the Eclipse’s points with everyone else. I also watched Saffron win the fourth quarter against a team that had beaten it in the regular season, with Skattebo extending the drive when the next snap was all it had left.

Give me Saffron 27, Mossdeep 24. I’m asking Scarboro to keep calling for the player who can gain eight to the right, then gain seven on the catch when the defense tightens up. Let Marino have the ball early enough to make the matchup good. On the possession that decides it, I want Scarboro giving No. 22 one more chance to take the clock with him.

art.alt: Saffron’s pink No. 22 jersey hangs above two cyan paths, one straight and one turning.

articles.author: rowan-vale
articles.title: Saffron can win the Bowl with Archam Manning and its pass rush
articles.dek: The Psi Corps have put up 118 points in three playoff games. NeMarcus Tare and Chen Norton Jr are making sure opponents have fewer good chances to answer.

body.text: Saffron has scored 42, 38 and 38 in its three playoff games. I had the Psi Corps second in my last rankings, where the first-place club had just won 40–3 and was still working on a rather large argument against dissent. My opening bracket picked Saffron to win the Bowl anyway. The team I picked has spent three rounds making me look cautious about its offense. Thirty-eight has become such a common result that the person changing the scoreboard could work from a rubber stamp.

Last week’s 38–27 win at Mt. Silver makes the case with more conviction than the wider playoff margins. The Reds won the clubs’ first game 36–33. In the rematch they erased a 14-point deficit, brought a punt back for a touchdown and led by six inside three minutes. Saffron had enough offense to take the lead back twice and enough defense to force two late turnovers on downs. Mossdeep will bring the better season record to the neutral site. Saffron brings the more persuasive evidence from the last two weeks that its defense can create time for another Manning touchdown.

Saffron’s losses came by one to Vermilion, three to Mossdeep and three to Mt. Silver. The Psi Corps have since won six straight and scored at least 31 in each. That’s a larger stretch of scoring than the playoff wins alone. The Psi Corps have kept scoring after the sort of close loss they took in Week 10, and the Mt. Silver rematch shows what happened when they got another chance.
Manning is scoring with the full receiving group

Saffron’s first two touchdown drives against Mt. Silver covered 64 and 93 yards. Archam Manning finished both with short throws to Gengar Pickens, one to the left for eleven yards and one to the right for eight. HeeDee Lamb’s 26-yard catch deep right helped the second drive cross the field. Then the Psi Corps punted on four consecutive offensive possessions. The same passing game later built scoring drives of 78 and 74 yards. Both the fast start and the long stretch of inactivity belong in the file. It says something encouraging about the offense that the second recovery was good enough to win a conference.

Look at the two games together. Manning threw for 281 yards and four touchdowns against Lavender and 254 and four against Mt. Silver. He threw no interceptions in either game. Lamb went for 123 yards against the Wails and 78 against the Reds. Bysson Witten caught two touchdowns in the first win. Pickens caught two in the second. Mothel Irving put a touchdown on the board against Lavender, and Woobat caught the 17-yarder that gave Saffron the lead at Mt. Silver. A defensive staff can walk into the week with a persuasive plan for Lamb and find five other invitations printed on the same piece of paper.
Pickens makes one play and that gives the next guy a little more room. He’d probably tell you he likes his room just fine. I’m happy to use all of it.
body.speaker: Archam Manning

body.text: Lamb’s zero-week minor injury entry is worth tracking, and fullback Emmitt Smoth’s three-week listing keeps him out. Lamb caught a 25-yard pass on third-and-six on Saffron’s first touchdown drive of the second half. He also caught the 16-yarder that set up Woobat’s score on the late go-ahead drive. Those receptions help explain why a defense tends to spend so much of the day aware of where he lines up. Mossdeep is already missing corner Marshall Flock for another week and allowed 157 receiving yards to FLOAT SZN last week. The jobs Lamb and FLOAT SZN do for their teams differ. The size of that line still puts a lot of the attention on what the Eclipse do the moment the ball gets into the hands of someone in space.
Tare and Norton can take away a drive on their own

NeMarcus Tare recorded five sacks against Lavender and four against Mt. Silver. Chen Norton Jr had two in each game. The Reds lost 33 yards on their six sacks and didn’t throw a pick. Saffron can change possession even when the other team makes the sensible quarterback decision. Norton’s sack on fourth-and-six at 0:50 gave the offense a short field late, which produced a 31-yard Octillery kick. Earlier, Tare sacked Jacoby Brizzet on first-and-five. Brizzet came back on second-and-eleven and threw the touchdown. That game contained both the price Saffron can impose and the response Marino is more than capable of making.

Saffron led the league with 78 regular-season sacks. Tare had 29 in thirteen games, and Norton had 23. Twenty-six belonged to the rest of the defense. Marino might use help for both linebackers and still find that a third rusher is the one who ends the series. Those two are the clearest reason Saffron can build its title case around creating its own extra possessions.

In the Week 10 game, Norton personally sacked Marino four times. Saffron was ahead 17–6 at halftime and won the day’s yardage comparison 334–314, and I am obliged by the existence of a second half to print that Mossdeep won 20–17. The Eclipse gave up zero points after the break. Marino drove 80 yards for the winner and Electric Berry intercepted Manning on Saffron’s first snap after the kick. The Psi Corps already applied enough pressure to make a championship case. They needed another scoring drive while they still had the lead.

Marino hasn’t thrown a playoff interception and threw four touchdown passes against Sunyshore. BeckhmJr caught the final one from 70 yards. The value of a first-down hit or an untimely incompletion against that offense is a better chance to keep the longest plays from getting a second try. Mossdeep’s route to winning is to use Ninjaskamara and the inside receivers so often that Saffron has to protect shorter yardage and give Marino more chances to find BeckhmJr late. Poury Holt still has three weeks to go, and Joey Sporeter shows zero weeks on a minor entry. Mossdeep has sufficient demonstrated production out of the available backfield to make that plan annoying.
Saffron’s offense has enough for another answer

The last two opponents showed two different ways to give Manning a difficult day. Lavender sacked him four times and got a safety. Mt. Silver made him go back out after a return fumble and then take two more possessions trailing. He finished with four scoring passes each time. That’s a good answer to what the Psi Corps lacked after halftime in Week 10, when the defense kept giving them another series and the offense never added a point.

My opening bracket said Saffron 30–27 against Mossdeep. My current pick is Saffron 35, Mossdeep 28. I expect Marino and BeckhmJr to collect on a clean pocket, and I expect Saffron to spend one more possession giving its quarterback a chance to answer. With Tare and Norton helping force punts and Manning finding more than one player who can finish, I’ll give the Psi Corps five touchdowns. Pickens can make his case for two of them.

art.alt: Alakazam in Saffron’s pink and cyan No. 6 jersey leans on a railing.

articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Flock remains out as the finalists review availability
articles.dek: Mossdeep and Saffron retain continuing absences; Mt. Silver adds three positive-week entries after the conference championships.

body.text: Marshall Flock remains listed with one week on his injury counter as Mossdeep prepares to face Saffron in the Indigo Bowl. The cornerback's counter has fallen from two since the previous report. Poury Holt remains on the report at three weeks, down from four. Both are continuing absences attached to earlier games.

Saffron's Emmitt Smoth is also listed for three weeks, down from four. The Psi Corps' conference-game additions include HeeDee Lamb with a minor entry and zero weeks remaining. Mossdeep's Joey Sporeter has the same reported duration on a new minor entry. Neither zero-week entry supports a new missed-game claim or an invented questionable designation.

Flock's availability matters to a Mossdeep defense preparing for Archam Manning, who threw four touchdowns against Mt. Silver. Lamb caught four passes for seventy-eight yards in that game. The distinction between an absent corner and a receiver with a zero-week entry matters to the championship preview, but neither the injury counter nor this report establishes the final defensive assignments.

Mt. Silver has three new injuries with time remaining after its conference loss: Crem Ftzpatrik at ten weeks, Roselia at four and Kevin Metwae at one. Crem attempted three passes; Jacoby Brizzet attempted thirty. Crem's final named snap in the passing sequence is a sack at 5:40 of the second quarter, and Brizzet's first named pass follows at 5:01. The report does not identify the injury's timing or cause.

The Reds also have two players whose counters reached zero: Tic Thorpe and Foo Warner, both previously listed for one week. That change records their current status; it does not demonstrate that either appeared in the conference championship. Gregar Jenings remains at five weeks, Ariados at seven, and Tony Gyarzalez at two.

Sunyshore's Don Philliams has a new three-week entry from the Mossdeep game. The Starseekers' continuing report includes 88 Special at thirteen weeks, reduced from fourteen. Sunyshore's elimination ends its title pursuit, while its players' reported recovery information remains part of the league-wide record.

Elsewhere, Palafin of Hearthome, Dusknoir of Oreburgh and Zangoose of Violet have counters that reached zero from one. The table includes every player with an injury entry in either weekly report and separates newly recorded injuries, ordinary countdown changes and cleared entries. These durations are the game's reported counters. They do not establish medical diagnoses, precise return dates or future starting roles.

articles.author: calvin-rook
articles.title: Iron Bundle leads the edge search; Throh sets the inside standard
articles.dek: Calvin Rook separates twelve linebackers by the work they would be asked to do, with Shalour’s movement star and Agate’s strongest reported range at the front.

body.text: Iron Bundle is the outside linebacker I want to examine first. Shalour Military Academy's prospect ran a 4.53 forty, jumped forty-seven inches and finished the cone in 5.96 seconds. Those results arrive beside a 69–97 scouting range. Agate State's Throh has the stronger reported range, 71–99, and is my first inside linebacker. Two jobs produce two starting points. A general manager should know which job is vacant before asking me for a single name.

The conference championships supplied a good reason to care about the distinction. Saffron's NeMarcus Tare made four sacks and Chen Norton Jr. added two. Mossdeep's Derrat Brooks produced the interception that gave his offense a nineteen-yard touchdown drive. These were different ways for linebackers to influence a close game. A prospect's combine can tell us something about movement and strength testing; it cannot award either professional performance in advance.

I have Iron Bundle first overall on this twelve-player list because its movement results are unusually persuasive within the group. Throh remains first for an inside vacancy. Mid-Galar State's Qwilfish gives the outside group a second candidate with a strong range and movement tests. Farther down, Lilycove's Bouffalant moves ahead of Ambrette's Pyukumuku on my board despite a slightly lower range. That is a judgment about the visible combination, and I am prepared to defend it.

Mossdeep and Saffron can watch the Bowl first and review their linebacker work afterward. Sunyshore, after allowing four passing touchdowns in its conference loss, should be asking how its coverage and pressure assignments interact before choosing a prospect to solve one of them. I would send teams needing an outside option to Shalour and Mid-Galar; for an inside vacancy, I would begin with Agate and Mahogany and make room for Lilycove. Those are scouting recommendations, not claims about a club's final draft position or a player's eventual availability.

The university names below distinguish prospects who share a species. Both Throh and both Octillery players have individual records, and the two Pyukumuku entries belong to different schools. The range endpoints are reported scouting bounds rather than guaranteed outcomes. I want more football evidence before making a final selection, but these are the twelve conversations I would start now.

prospects.name: Iron Bundle
prospects.analysis: Iron Bundle gives me the most compelling outside-linebacker movement profile on this board: a 4.53 forty, 47-inch vertical and 5.96 cone, with seventeen bench repetitions. Shalour Military Academy's prospect also carries a 69–97 range, close to the strongest reported range in the group. I would start my edge search here, especially if I needed the same player to threaten space and change direction rather than simply run straight ahead.
prospects.concern: The workout cannot establish how quickly Iron Bundle will recognize routes or finish a blocked rush. Those remain football questions.
prospects.projection: My first outside-linebacker evaluation, with a movement profile worth investigating for a varied role.

prospects.name: Throh
prospects.analysis: Agate State's Throh owns the strongest reported range among these twelve, 71–99. The 5.05 forty and 7.02 cone give a different picture from Iron Bundle's workout; eighteen bench repetitions add a solid strength result. A club shopping for an inside linebacker should begin with Throh instead of pretending that two different positions need the same ordering.
prospects.concern: The twenty-eight-point range remains broad. Its upper endpoint is not a promised finished player.
prospects.projection: First inside linebacker on my board and a priority evaluation for teams seeking work between the tackles.

prospects.name: Qwilfish
prospects.analysis: Mid-Galar State's Qwilfish combines a 67–95 range with a 4.81 forty, forty-one-inch vertical and 6.42 cone. Seventeen bench reps match Iron Bundle's total. The movement results give me a second outside-linebacker option with a clear argument of its own, even though Iron Bundle's times and jump lead this comparison.
prospects.concern: The tests favor Iron Bundle in this pairing; Qwilfish needs a role-specific football evaluation to close the gap.
prospects.projection: Second edge option here, worth comparing closely with the leading player rather than treating as a consolation choice.

prospects.name: Throh
prospects.analysis: University of Mahogany's Throh brings twenty bench reps and a 65–93 range. The forty and cone, 5.07 and 7.04, sit close to Agate State's Throh. At twenty-one, this is also a younger prospect than the twenty-three-year-old Agate player. These are two separate evaluations, with different reported ranges and strength results, despite sharing a species.
prospects.concern: Age and two extra repetitions cannot settle a six-point difference at both range endpoints.
prospects.projection: My second inside-linebacker conversation, especially for a club willing to spend more evaluation time on the uncertainty.

prospects.name: Bouffalant
prospects.analysis: Lilycove's Bouffalant makes a persuasive case for moving ahead of a higher-range prospect. The 63–91 range comes with twenty bench reps, a 4.96 forty and 6.96 cone. I like that combination for an inside-linebacker discussion. There is enough strength-test performance to keep the movement numbers from being the entire sales pitch, and enough movement to make me ask about more than a stationary interior role.
prospects.concern: A pleasing combination of tests does not prove a complete linebacker, and the range trails both Throh prospects.
prospects.projection: My third inside option; Lilycove deserves an early visit from any club comparing physical approaches in the middle.

prospects.name: Pyukumuku
prospects.analysis: Ambrette Naval Academy's Pyukumuku has a 64–92 range, a point above Bouffalant at both ends. Its 5.23 forty, 7.17 cone and fourteen bench reps push me toward the Lilycove player first. This is where my ordering becomes a football preference rather than a simple sort of the reported range. I would still keep Ambrette's prospect in the next group of inside-linebacker evaluations.
prospects.concern: The slower movement tests need a convincing intended role; the reported range alone cannot answer that concern.
prospects.projection: An inside candidate for a team prepared to examine anticipation and assignment fit closely.

prospects.name: Mawile
prospects.analysis: University of Cyllage's Mawile is my next outside linebacker. The 62–90 range matches Sableye's, while the 4.98 forty, 6.89 cone and thirty-five-inch vertical beat that direct comparison. Fourteen bench repetitions are the same for both. Those small but consistent workout edges give me an initial preference without pretending I have watched either prospect solve a professional protection.
prospects.concern: The top two outside prospects have stronger reported ranges and substantially better movement results.
prospects.projection: A second group edge evaluation with a straightforward workout advantage over the next player.

prospects.name: Sableye
prospects.analysis: Porto Marinada Coastal's Sableye shares Mawile's 62–90 range and fourteen bench reps. A 5.07 forty, 6.96 cone and thirty-three-inch vertical leave it behind Cyllage's prospect on my first pass. I would keep the two together in the evaluation schedule because matching reported ranges leave room for the football assessment to change their order.
prospects.concern: Nothing in the current tests supports placing Sableye ahead of Mawile on athletic performance alone.
prospects.projection: Outside-linebacker depth candidate to compare directly with Cyllage's Mawile.

prospects.name: Octillery
prospects.analysis: University of Violet's Octillery offers a 61–89 range, eighteen bench reps, a 5.02 forty and 7.05 cone. Its strength and movement results sit within the broad inside-linebacker conversation rather than standing out like Iron Bundle's edge workout. That can still be useful: a club that misses the leading inside prospects needs a coherent next evaluation, not an invented guarantee.
prospects.concern: The leading Throh has a ten-point advantage at both endpoints; Violet's prospect needs more than a familiar set of tests to erase it.
prospects.projection: The first Octillery I would examine, with a higher reported range than Cherrygrove's separate prospect.

prospects.name: Octillery
prospects.analysis: University of Cherrygrove's Octillery counters with nineteen bench reps and a thirty-six-inch vertical, compared with Violet's eighteen and thirty-two. Its 59–87 range is lower, while a 5.05 forty and 7.03 cone split the movement comparison. The result is a useful pair to study together. I favor Violet on the range, but Cherrygrove has specific testing advantages worth asking about.
prospects.concern: A better jump and one additional repetition do not establish superior play strength or a better overall prospect.
prospects.projection: An inside-linebacker alternative whose workout warrants a direct comparison with Violet.

prospects.name: Pincurchin
prospects.analysis: University of Pewter's Pincurchin joins the board with a 59–87 range and eighteen bench repetitions. A 5.19 forty and 7.19 cone create a clear movement concern relative to several inside options above it. I would want the assignment to be well defined before moving this player ahead of a more mobile candidate. The strength result earns a closer look without resolving that tradeoff.
prospects.concern: The current workout offers less evidence for a broad space role than the quicker inside prospects provide.
prospects.projection: A narrower inside-linebacker evaluation, with the team's intended job driving its interest.

prospects.name: Pyukumuku
prospects.analysis: Vermilion Metropolitan's Pyukumuku shares Pincurchin's 59–87 range but records eleven bench reps, a 5.28 forty and a 7.28 cone. Among this selected group, those results leave the clearest physical questions. I would ask what additional football evidence changes the comparison before paying for the same reported range that other prospects pair with stronger workouts.
prospects.concern: The visible record provides little reason to move it ahead of the inside alternatives listed here.
prospects.projection: Later evaluation priority on this board; a role-specific case would have to emerge from further scouting.
